thread:
noah-marketing: quick help please. we're finalizing a launch post + a webinar demo and need a reproducible bench pack from runtime for the rw-7B-q4-v2 long-context campaign. main asks:
- per-request + per-token traces for seq lenses 1k/4k/8k (coldstart, warmed)
- throughput curves (tokens/sec) vs tail latency (p95/p99) at 1,2,4,8 batch sizes
- outlier capture: any requests >3x median latency and the anonymized prompt
- exact run artifacts: bench client binary hash, runtime git sha, kernel/cuda versions, batcher config, quant flags, seeds
- small methodology brief (2 bullets + 3-para one-pager) that marketing can quote in the blog
- packaging: traces.tar.gz, csvs/{seq_len}_percentiles.csv, checksums.sha256, marketing-samples.txt

Can runtime produce this by Wed EOD so we can lock the PR? noah will coordinate legal redaction if needed. cc @tala-runtime @sam-eng

tala-runtime: we can do this. couple clarifications: do you want raw protobuf traces or json lines? how many "marketing samples" do you need in marketing-samples.txt? also, what qualifies as "coldstart" in your charts (first request after model load or after idle > X minutes)?

noah-marketing: jsonl is perfect. include full per-request metadata but scrub PII. marketing-samples.txt: 5 anonymized input/output pairs with the gen config used. coldstart = first request after model loaded (we'll note idle >5min in the brief).

sam-eng: runtime plan:
- today: smoke harness to ensure traces and csv exporters work (30m)
- tomorrow 08:30 UTC: full sweep across seq lens [1024,4096,8192] x batch sizes [1,2,4,8] on a 4-node A100 pool
- capture: per-token latency, batch occupancy timeline, kv-cache hit markers, GPU mem timeline, outlier flagging
- produce: csvs with p50/p90/p95/p99, tokens_per_sec curves, and jsonl traces.

sam-eng: run snippet (example):
```bash
# warmup script (pseudo)
./bench_client --model rw-7B-q4-v2 --seq_len 4096 --batch 4 --warmup_steps 50 --seed 2026 --trace-out traces/ --metrics-out csvs/

# full sweep (simplified)
./bench_sweep --model rw-7B-q4-v2 --seqs 1024,4096,8192 --batches 1,2,4,8 --seed-file seeds.txt --jsonl-out traces/run.jsonl --metrics-dir csvs/
```

jun-product: tiny request for the methodology brief: include a short section on variance sources (tokenizer mismatch, NDP ops, clock skew) and the mitigation steps you took so marketing can cite "controlled for X" in the blog. also add a one-line about reproducibility: "seeds+hashes included".

tala-runtime: noted. we'll capture git hashes for bench_client, runtime, tokenizer, and kernel versions. we'll also include a quick rerun checklist so someone can reproduce the exact run locally.

bench-bot: scheduled job brq4-launchpack-2026-03-25-0830. estimated run time 3h. artifacts will go to s3://redwood-marketing/launchpacks/rw-7B-q4-v2/2026-03-25-0830/ with retention 60d.

noah-marketing: perfect. one more: could you include checksums and a tiny verification script (verify_checksums.sh) so marketing can validate artifacts before sharing externally?

tala-runtime: yes, will add verify_checksums.sh and a marketing-readme with 5 anonymized samples + explicit gen config per-sample. we'll mark any nondet ops we couldn't fully pin and explain the likely impact in the brief.

sam-eng: tagging ops for bucket ACLs and marketing read-only link: @ops please ensure marketing team has read access to s3 path.

noah-marketing: thanks all. hitting sync with comms tomorrow after you upload. :rocket:
